list: The official 55 trophies, as listed before this guide was built. Names, descriptions and grades are PlayStation's own words; every guide below is written for this entry, in our own words, from the official description. Where a place or a step cannot be pinned down from the description, the guide says so plainly instead of guessing.
sourcesNote: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count where one is tracked); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: This is the payoff, not a task of its own: it unlocks when the other 54 trophies are earned, so the whole guide is the guide to it. Work the roadmap in order — story first, then side strands, activities, collectibles, and the heist and robbery cleanup last — and check the Next Up planner whenever you are unsure what to chase next. Nothing here needs a special trick; it needs the full list done.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end. It is the first mission of the game, so there is nothing to prepare and nothing to miss — just follow the mission as it unfolds and let the story carry you through. If you are trophy hunting from the start, tick this one off and move on to Chapter 1.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1. Chapter trophies come from story progress alone, so the practical advice is pacing: do not rush past side content you enjoy, but know that nothing in Chapter 1 itself is gated behind collectibles. Clear the chapter, bank the trophy, and keep the save moving forward.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies it is pure story progress, earned by playing through rather than by hunting anything. Use the chapter as a natural checkpoint: before moving on, glance at the missables page, since later chapters hold the one-chance moments this chapter does not.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3. By now the pattern is set: chapter trophies track the story, not your skill, so the only way to lose time here is to stall. Keep pushing the main missions and let the side strands wait for stage 2 of the roadmap, where they get their own pass.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale, so treat it as the end of stage 1: story done except the final mission. Before the finale, check the missables page once — the final stretch is where one-chance trophies cluster, and a quick look now costs less than a replay later.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete the final mission. It is a gold trophy because it closes the story, not because it is hard to find — reach the end and finish it. Do the missable cleanup first if you can: anything tied to a single moment in the finale is easier to attempt on the way in than to chase after the credits. Not yet checked in the game whether the final mission can be replayed.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Breakfast Run. Named-mission trophies like this one are earned by finishing that mission, so the guide is simple: play the mission when the story offers it and see it through to the end. If a mission ever feels failed, retry it from the mission itself rather than reloading an old save and losing progress elsewhere.
trophies.name: Trust
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions tend to be longer than ordinary ones, so go in with full health and supplies if the game lets you prepare, and follow the mission's own objectives instead of improvising. The trophy is for completion, so a clean finish beats a flashy one.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Child's Play. The mission's name is the only clue the official description gives, and that is enough: it unlocks through story progress, and finishing it is the whole requirement. No side task is attached to it, so do not go hunting for one.
trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Headliners. As with the other named-mission trophies, the work is the mission itself: reach it in the story and finish it. Keep a manual save from before big story missions if you like a safety net, but the description gives no extra condition to prepare for.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission VCIA Takedown. The name points at Vice City International Airport, so expect an airport set piece, but the trophy itself only asks for completion. Finish the mission and the trophy follows; anything fancier than that is a bonus, not a requirement. Not yet checked in the game how the takedown itself plays out.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Operation Savage Glory. Operation names usually mean a large set-piece mission, so take your time with it and use cover and the mission's own checkpoints. The trophy is for finishing, so surviving the operation matters more than doing it stylishly.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own completion tracker. This is the long tail of the platinum: story, side strands, activities, collectibles and the rest all feed the same percentage, so it usually lands near the end of a full playthrough rather than on its own. Use this guide's checklist as a stand-in for the in-game tracker, and treat the last few percent as cleanup — the remaining trophies will tell you what is left.
trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts in total — the count is cumulative, so every stunt you pull anywhere in Leonida counts toward it. The practical approach is to let it build passively while you play, then grind the remainder late: jumps, near-misses and air time all feed the same counter, and repeating a reliable stunt beats hunting new ones. Not yet checked in the game which moves count as stunts or whether any stunt type is excluded.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 250); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once — all 9 types, one try each. The trick is breadth, not depth: sample everything the game offers (races, fishing, arcade, bowling, the shooting range and the rest) instead of grinding one favourite. Keep a mental checklist as you go; the moment you have tried the last type, the trophy pops. Not yet checked in the game which 9 types the counter recognises.
trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 9); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Work through them one weapon at a time and chase gold on each; a single silver or bronze leaves the trophy locked, so revisit the ones you missed rather than replaying the ones you aced. Treat it as a late-game cleanup pass once you are comfortable with each weapon type — the bar is gold in all 42, and no shortcut is stated. Not yet checked in the game whether challenges can be retried freely.
trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 42); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every one of the 14 locations. Each location needs its own win, so the work is a tour: clear one location, move to the next, and tick them off in this guide as you go. Drone racing rewards clean lines over raw speed, so learn each course's turns before pushing for the win. Not yet checked in the game where the 14 locations are.
trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 14); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different is the key word, so replaying your favourite race twenty times will not do it. Spread out across race types and locations, and use the wins you already have from story and side content as a head start. Keep the count visible in this guide and pick the easiest un-won races first when you are close to 20.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 20); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are usually about patience and timing rather than gear, so watch Cal's rhythm and the challenge's own prompts instead of rushing. The description names one opponent and one challenge, so this is a single event to win, not a grind. Not yet checked in the game whether the challenge can be retried if you lose it.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Any arcade game counts, so pick the shortest or easiest one you find and play it through rather than sampling several. It pairs naturally with Master of None, which wants you to try every activity type once — the arcade is one of those types.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy. Side strands like Andy's are chains: each mission unlocks the next, so keep returning to the strand's contact whenever new missions appear instead of leaving it half done. The trophy is for the last mission in the chain, so follow the strand to its end and do not skip its earlier steps.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton. Work through Kenton's strand mission by mission; the final one only appears after the earlier ones are done, so a strand that looks finished early probably is not. Check the roadmap's stage 2 list if you are unsure whether a contact still has missions left.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy. Billy's strand is one of several named contacts with a final-mission trophy, and the pattern is the same for all of them: finish the chain, and the trophy lands on the last mission. Do the strands in stage 2, after the story, so nothing interrupts the chain halfway through.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Stranger strands are the open-world side missions you find by exploring, not by following the story, so this one rewards wandering: answer the stranger prompts you meet and see each strand through. Eight is the target, and the named contacts in stage 2 (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone, Bret) are a good start — the rest come from strangers you meet on the road.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 8); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy. Randy's strand follows the same rule as the other contacts: the final mission is the payoff for finishing the chain. If Randy goes quiet for a while, play more story or explore — strands often unlock their next step after other progress. Not yet checked in the game what triggers each step.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone. Finish Tyrone's strand end to end, and keep it with the other contact strands in stage 2 so the whole set is done in one pass. Like the other strand trophies it is about persistence — the chain, not any single mission, is the work.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every one of the 18 spots across Leonida. Meditation spots are a collectible in all but name: the work is finding all 18, so tour the map systematically and tick each spot off in this guide as you visit it. Do them in stage 3 with the other activities, when you are travelling the map anyway. Not yet checked in the game where the 18 spots are.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 18); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. This is a hunting strand, not a random encounter: follow Bret's strand until the hunt itself is offered, then take the shot the hunt asks for. Unique animals are usually one of a kind, so do not waste the attempt on a rushed shot — wait for a clean one. Not yet checked in the game which animal it is or where the hunt takes place.
trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets. Cards are scattered collectibles, so this is a long hunt: pick up every card you pass, and only chase the last few sets once you know which cards you are missing. Three full sets is the target, not three cards, so expect to collect far more than three cards in total. Not yet checked in the game how many cards a set holds or where they are.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 3); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations — the count is the whole challenge, so make it a habit: use the WAiNK feature wherever you go instead of saving it for a dedicated session. One hundred is a lot, so fold it into normal play and let the number climb while you do everything else. Not yet checked in the game what counts as a WAiNK location or whether repeats count.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 100); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's small objectives layered over normal play, so the fastest route is variety: try different activities, vehicles and approaches and let the completions stack up. The counter is cumulative, so nothing is wasted — but do check which challenges you have already finished before grinding one type. Not yet checked in the game how challenges are listed in-game.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 50); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. MISSABLE in spirit: the setup is specific, so plan it — get your partner with you, build the wanted level to exactly 4 stars, then break line of sight and stay hidden until it clears. Do it deliberately, not by accident: a random 4-star chase with no partner nearby wastes the attempt. Not yet checked in the game whether the partner must be present for the whole escape.
trophies.missableReason: Needs a 4-star wanted level lost with your partner present — a specific setup that can pass you by if you escape alone or at the wrong wanted level.
trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level. MISSABLE: the chain is the challenge — three robberies in a row, partner beside you, wanted level held the whole time. Pick three shops close together, plan the route before the first robbery, and do not stop to fight or browse between them. If the wanted level drops, the chain breaks and you start over.
trophies.missableReason: Three robberies back-to-back with your partner, wanted level held throughout — one break in the chain and the attempt is over.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Discovery is passive — every new vehicle you drive or encounter counts — so the number climbs on its own while you play, and the remainder is a matter of variety: try new vehicle types instead of sticking to one favourite. It pairs with On the Spot, which wants 10 vehicles registered, so register the interesting ones as you find them.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 100); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. MISSABLE in practice: you need five enemies close together and one Combat Focus window, so set it up — find a group, wait until they cluster, then trigger it and work fast. Do not waste Combat Focus on one or two stragglers; save it for a crowd. Not yet checked in the game how long Combat Focus lasts or how it recharges.
trophies.missableReason: Five takedowns inside one Combat Focus use — needs a group of enemies and a single well-timed activation.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA (Vice City International Airport). MISSABLE: this is a one-off stunt at a specific place, not something that happens in normal play — go to the airport deliberately and leave in a way the game does not schedule. Save before you try it, so a failed attempt costs you nothing. Not yet checked in the game what counts as an unscheduled departure.
trophies.missableReason: A single unscheduled departure at VCIA — a one-off moment at one place, easy to walk past without trying it.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Deal with the Rhinos — the description is a joke, not an instruction, so read it as a hint that tanks (Rhinos) are involved. The honest guide is short: when a Rhino encounter comes up, take it on rather than avoiding it, and expect a fight that wants heavy weapons or a clever route, not a head-on charge. Not yet checked in the game what the encounter is or whether it repeats.
trophies.missableReason: The description names Rhinos but no repeatable trigger — treat the encounter as one-off until the game proves otherwise.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. MISSABLE: stealth is the whole requirement, so plan the robbery like a quiet job — go in prepared, avoid cameras and sightlines, and leave before anyone raises the alarm. One detection ends the attempt, so save beforehand and retry the approach, not the whole game. Not yet checked in the game which jewelry store the description means.
trophies.missableReason: One detection ends the attempt — a stealth robbery with no second chance inside the same try.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Rob 5 Bank Vaults and escape — all five, each with a getaway. Bank vaults are bigger jobs than shop robberies, so prepare each one: know your exit before you go in, and do not linger after the vault is open. The count is cumulative across vaults, so clear them one at a time in stage 5. Not yet checked in the game where the 5 vaults are.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 5); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an Armored Truck and escape. Armored trucks are roaming targets, so the job is in two parts: find one and stop it, then get away clean. Do not open the truck in the open if you can help it — move it somewhere quieter first, and have your getaway planned before the doors open. The escape counts as much as the robbery.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. This is the map-completion trophy: every area counts, so the work is coverage, not speed. Travel the edges of the map deliberately — the areas you never visit are the ones that hold this trophy back — and tick areas off as you pass through them. It overlaps with the collectible hunts in stage 4, so do them together.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 52); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. One operation per gang, nine in total — the challenge is coverage, not repetition, so do not rob the same gang's operation twice and call it progress. Learn which operations belong to which gang as you find them, and keep a per-gang tally in this guide. Not yet checked in the game how gang ownership is shown.
trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 9); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is a moment trophy, not a challenge: go to Ocean Beach, find a place that serves a cocktail with a view, and take the moment. It is a good palate cleanser between harder trophies — cheap, quick and impossible to fail once you are in the right place. Not yet checked in the game which venue the description means.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. MISSABLE: this is a set-piece moment — a showroom, a vehicle, and a smash exit — so it reads as a one-time scene rather than a repeatable activity. When you find yourself in a vehicle showroom, look for the dramatic exit before the quiet one. Not yet checked in the game which showroom it is or whether the moment repeats.
trophies.missableReason: A showroom smash exit reads as a one-time set piece — easy to miss by taking the ordinary way out.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Bowling is one of the activity types, so this trophy is really about finding the alley and playing a proper game there — follow through on your throw, as the name says. It pairs with Ten Pin, the melee drive-by trophy, only in name; the two are separate jobs. Not yet checked in the game where the alley is.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Build a partnership with mass appeal. The description is deliberately vague — it names a partnership and an audience, but no action — so the honest guide is: play the partner content as it comes, and watch for a moment where the partnership itself is the point. MISSABLE in spirit: a partnership moment may only happen once, so do not skip partner scenes. Not yet checked in the game what triggers it.
trophies.missableReason: The description gives no repeatable trigger — a partnership moment that may only happen once, so do not skip partner scenes.
trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks a count to 500, so this is a long-haul trophy about deciding, not about deciding right. Every choice in dialogue and missions feeds it, so just keep playing and choosing; it will land on its own over a full playthrough. MISSABLE only in the sense that choices cannot be unmade — but the count is what matters, not any single choice, so do not agonise over one. Not yet checked in the game which choices count.
trophies.missableReason: Choices cannot be unmade — the count to 500 is cumulative, but any single choice is final.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 500); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try. The description implies a failure followed by a success, so this trophy is about retrying: when something goes wrong, try again instead of reloading an old save. MISSABLE in spirit — a perfect first-time run through everything would never trigger it — so do not fear failing once. Not yet checked in the game which event it attaches to.
trophies.missableReason: It needs a second try after a failure — a perfect first-time run would never trigger it.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Witness something strange. This is the game's weird-event trophy: something unusual happens, and being there is the whole requirement. Keep your eyes open while exploring — strange events usually happen in strange places, off the main roads. MISSABLE in spirit: a one-off event can pass while you are looking the other way. Not yet checked in the game what the event is or where it happens.
trophies.missableReason: A one-off strange event — it can pass while you are looking the other way.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by. MISSABLE in practice: you need a moving vehicle, a melee weapon, and a target close enough to hit from it — three things that rarely line up by accident. Set it up deliberately on a quiet road with a slow target, and save first so a miss costs nothing. Not yet checked in the game which weapons count as melee for a drive-by.
trophies.missableReason: Needs a vehicle, a melee weapon and a target lined up at once — a setup that rarely happens by accident.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists, so this trophy feeds off the stage 5 cleanup: keep robbing, keep laundering, and let the total climb. Use your contacts to move the money rather than sitting on it — the count is the amount laundered, not the amount held. Not yet checked in the game which contacts launder or what the rate is.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 250000); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. This one takes care of itself if you play normally — weapons, clothes, vehicles and supplies all count toward the same total. Do not force it early by buying junk; let it build, and only top it up deliberately near the end with purchases you actually want. The total is cumulative across every shop.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase official list (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 100000); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Garages are bought, not found, so this is a money trophy in disguise: save up, then buy them one by one. It pairs with Whip It Good (discover 100 vehicles) — garages give your collection somewhere to live. Check prices before you start, and buy the cheapest first so the set shrinks fast.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Find ten vehicles worth keeping, open the Scooter Bros app, and register each one — ten registrations is the target, and any ten vehicles will do. Do it alongside Whip It Good, which wants 100 vehicles discovered: register the best of each batch as you find them, and the two trophies move together.
